'''André Haefliger''' ({{IPA|de-CH|ˈandreː ˈhɛːflɪɡər}}; 22 May 1929{{dash}}7 March 2023) was a Swiss mathematician who worked primarily on [[topology]].

== Education and career ==
Haefliger went to school in [[Nyon]] and then attended his final years at [[Collège Calvin|Collège de Genève]] in [[Geneva]]. He studied mathematics at the [[University of Lausanne]] from 1948 to 1952. He worked for two years as a teaching assistant at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|École Polytechnique de l'Université de Lausanne]]. He then moved to [[University of Strasbourg]], then he followed [[Charles Ehresmann]] in Paris, where he received his [[Ph.D.]] degree in 1958.<ref>[[Max-Albert Knus]], [https://hls-dhs-dss.ch/fr/articles/043119/2011-01-06 'André Haefliger'], ''Historical Dictionary of Switzerland'', retrieved 22 March 2023.</ref> His thesis was entitled "''Structures feuilletées et cohomologie à valeurs dans un faisceau de groupoïdes''" and was written under the supervision of [[Charles Ehresmann]].<ref name="MG">{{MathGenealogy|id=28275}}</ref>

Haefliger got a [[research fellowship]] for one year at the [[University of Paris]], where he participated in the [[French mathematical seminars|seminar]] of [[Henri Cartan]], and then from 1959 to 1961 he worked at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]]. Since 1962 he has been a full professor at the [[University of Geneva]] until his retirement in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celebratio Mathematica — Haefliger — Jackson|url=https://celebratio.org/Haefliger_A/article/705/|access-date=19 December 2021|website=celebratio.org|language=en}}</ref>

In 1966 Haefliger was [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#1966, Moscow|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Moscow.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU)|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=&order=field_speakers_congress_city&sort=asc&page=83|access-date=19 December 2021|website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref> In 1974–75, he was president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Organisation » Past Presidents {{!}} The Swiss Mathematical Society|url=https://www.math.ch/organisation/past-presidents/|access-date=18 December 2021|website=www.math.ch}}</ref>

Haefliger obtained a Doctorate ''[[honoris causa]]'' from the [[Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zürich|ETH Zurich]] in 1992 and from the [[University of Dijon]] in 1997. In 2020 Haefliger and [[Martin Bridson]] were awarded the American Mathematical Society's [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition, for their book ''Metric Spaces of Non-Positive Curvature'' (Springer Verlag, 1999).<ref>{{Cite web|title=News from the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/tools/news?news_id=5574|access-date=18 December 2021|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref>

Haefliger died on 7 March 2023, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web |title=In memoriam André Haefliger |url=https://www.unige.ch/math/la-une/memoriam-andre-haefliger |website=Université de Genève |date=9 March 2023 |access-date=12 March 2023}}</ref>

== Research ==
Haefliger's main research interests were [[differential topology]] and [[Differential geometry|geometry]].

Haefliger found the topological obstruction to the existence of a [[spin structure]] on an [[Orientability|orientable]] [[Riemannian manifold]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=A. Haefliger|year=1956|title=Sur l'extension du groupe structural d'un espace fibré|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|volume=243|pages=558–560}}</ref> In two papers in the [[Annals of Mathematics|Annals]] he studied various [[embedding]] of [[sphere]]s in relations to [[knot theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Haefliger|first=Andre|date=1962|title=Knotted (4k - 1)-Spheres in 6k-Space|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1970208|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=75|issue=3|pages=452–466|doi=10.2307/1970208|jstor=1970208 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Haefliger|first=Andre|date=1966|title=Differentiable Embeddings of Sn in Sn+q for $q > 2$|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1970475|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=83|issue=3|pages=402–436|doi=10.2307/1970475|jstor=1970475 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He has also made important contributions in the theory of [[foliation]]s, introducing the notion of [[Haefliger structure]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Haefliger|first=A.|date=1970|title=Feuilletages sur les variétés ouvertes|journal=Topology|language=en|volume=9|issue=2|pages=183–194|doi=10.1016/0040-9383(70)90040-6|doi-access=}}</ref>

[[File:Eckmann Hilton Serre Haefliger.jpg|thumb|From left to right: [[Beno Eckmann]], [[Peter Hilton]], [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], and André Haefliger in [[Zürich]] in 2007]]
He wrote more than 80 papers in peer review journals<ref>{{Cite web|title=zbMATH Open - the first resource for mathematics|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=ai:haefliger.andre|access-date=19 December 2021|website=zbmath.org}}</ref> and had 20 Ph.D. students, including [[Augustin Banyaga]] and the future [[Fields Medal|Field Medalist]] [[Vaughan Jones]].<ref name="MG" />
